summary.headline: Runwal Enterprises Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 3,400 million (from Rs 4,462 million) on occupation-certificate-based recognition, while pre-sales rose ~5% to Rs 4,835 million.
summary.overview: This was the maiden earnings call after the company's listing, with the IPO proceeds received in the first week of October 2026. Pre-sales rose about 5% YoY to Rs 4,835 million and collections rose to Rs 5,754 million from Rs 4,993 million. Revenue from operations declined to about Rs 3,400 million, which management attributed to revenue being recognised only on occupation certificate and possession. Management said debt has been cut to about Rs 1,900 million external debt post-IPO and debt-to-equity has fallen from about 3 to about 1.5, with fuller benefits visible from Q3.

segments.name: Residential (Mumbai/MMR)
segments.commentary: Sold about 0.35 million sq ft in Q1 at an average selling price of about Rs 14,200 per sq ft, up significantly YoY, which management linked to the luxury mix. Delivered about 1 million sq ft in the quarter against occupation-certificate towers.

segments.name: Annuity / commercial
segments.commentary: Runwal BKC (about 0.31 million sq ft GLA) and Nexus Runwal Garden City Mall (about 0.75 million sq ft GLA) expected to complete in about 2.5 years; mall rental could exceed Rs 100 crore in the first year after stabilisation. Annuity income is currently minimal.

guidance_outlook: Management's endeavour is pre-sales growth of around 20% YoY, with 20-25% cited for the next two to three years; no formal numeric guidance given.
Long-term project-level EBITDA margin expected at upwards of 25%, sustained above 25% over the next few years; company-level EBITDA margin target of about 28% mentioned.
Interest saving of about Rs 50-60 crore per year expected from debt reduction, visible mainly from Q3 FY27 results.
Launch pipeline active for the next 12-15 months; management aims to grow pre-sales about 25% YoY with corresponding launch volumes, subject to approvals.

Post-IPO external debt about Rs 1,900 million; group-company related-party loans about Rs 365 million remain; the Rs 2,700 million total is expected to be about Rs 2,200 million in the Dec-quarter results.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio about 88 million sq ft (about 20 million ongoing, 56 million upcoming); total developable area about 88.4 million sq ft, of which about 74.6 million sq ft residential and about 6.37 million sq ft commercial.
Running projects have cumulative sales of about Rs 150,542 million, with collections of about Rs 114,280 million, leaving about Rs 36,000 million of receivables from sold area.
Two Dombivli integrated township platforms; Kalyan-Dombivli and eastern suburbs positioning cited.
Approvals pending for a Bandra society redevelopment and a Marine Drive project; Kanjurmarg and Bandra commercial opportunities under evaluation.
Proceeds of about Rs 325 crore from IPO used to repay debt; about Rs 500-600 crore total debt reduction including HDFC Capital CCD conversion.
demand_pricing: Management said prices in Dombivli, Kanjurmarg and Mulund belt carry a 3-5% premium over competitors and expects this to persist.
7 Mahalaxmi (South Mumbai luxury) priced at par with competition, with increases expected on upper floors as construction progresses.
Average selling price expected to keep rising as mix shifts to luxury and mid-income; land bank currently selling at around Rs 13,000 per sq ft.
Runwal ranked third in Mumbai for new residential launches (sales) between CY23 and Q1 CY27, first in eastern suburbs by sales and first in Kalyan-Dombivli by launches.
Company will stay MMR-focused with no plans to expand beyond the region for now.

qa_highlights.question: Strategic priorities for the next 2-3 years and expected growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Subodh Runwal cited growth in Mumbai at close to 20% CAGR, asset-light opportunities, margin focus and debt reduction. Management said its endeavour is about 20% YoY pre-sales growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company issue stated guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna Kanodia said no specific guidance yet, but a general direction on growth (20-25% pre-sales) will be given while maintaining balance-sheet and margin health.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment plan and current debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said debt-to-equity fell from 3.1x to 1.5x and debt is now about Rs 1,900 crore external. Future borrowing will be limited and self-liquidating. Shashi Bhushan added that land monetisation to data operators is being considered, with JLL mandated and 10-12 interested parties.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the land for the data-centre monetisation and how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashi Bhushan said the land is in Dombivli (Gardens and My City, part of a 250-acre parcel); about 18 acres is being considered for sale. No transaction has been concluded.

qa_highlights.question: Lease income profile from BKC and Nexus mall?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said both projects should complete in about 2.5 years, with mall rentals possibly above Rs 100 crore in year one after stabilisation. BKC tenant is still being sought; a rental number is hard to give at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Launch pipeline and approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashi Bhushan said two or three projects await approval, including a Bandra redevelopment and a Marine Drive project, likely launched this year or early next year. Management declined to give launch guidance because approvals are third-party dependent.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the IPO size cut from Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said SEBI offered a one-time option to halve offer size for entities already approved, given weak markets; the offer was all primary (about 10-11% dilution), and bankers advised taking it.

risks_watch: Revenue and EBITDA are lumpy because recognition depends on occupation certificates and possession; Q1 revenue fell about 24% YoY.
Launch timing depends on third-party approvals (Bandra, Marine Drive); no launch guidance given.
Debt reduction benefits (Rs 50-60 crore annual interest saving) and the post-IPO debt figure are only visible from the Dec-quarter results.
Possible data-centre land sale (about 18 acres in Dombivli) is not concluded; timing and pricing unknown.
Annuity income from BKC and the Nexus mall is about 2.5 years away and tenants for BKC are not yet finalised.
IPO was reduced from Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 500 crore; the company cited market conditions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and debt reduction, but cautious and evasive on launch timing, approvals and quantified annuity income. Management repeatedly deferred numbers to later quarters.

our endeavor would be in the range of 20% year-on-year.
The rental income from the mall could be on stabilization upwards of Rs. 100 crores in the first year.
